prize_parts.citation: for unifying electronic-structure calculation with the motion of atoms in first-principles molecular dynamics

statement.case_for: I move my first choice from B012 to B024. Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics is one dated, two-author 1985 step that was independently reproduced and used for four decades, and it made bond breaking, proton transfer and reactions in water and at surfaces computable without a fitted force field. Several colleagues, in particular Linke, Aqvist and Brzezinski, asked what in the Solexa chemistry could not have been replaced by competing routes. I cannot answer that from the record, and I have not verified the invention chronology. When I cannot defend a claim from the evidence, I should not make it the prize. The B024 citation can be anchored to the 1985 unification, so later metadynamics and machine-learned potentials need not be adjudicated. Its reach into biochemistry, through enzyme active sites and proton transfer, is indirect but real.
statement.case_against: B024 is a method prize with no experimental or biological counterpart, and it sits close to condensed-matter physics. Computational work was recognised in 2013 and 2024, and in everyday use Born-Oppenheimer dynamics and machine-learned potentials now do much of what the method did. My biological colleagues may rightly feel that the sequencing and degrader candidacies reach further into medicine. Sequencing by synthesis still strikes me as the larger change to what experimentalists can measure, and I do not retract that. My move reflects credit that cannot be settled, not a judgement that sequencing matters less.

responses.point: Brzezinski argues that B024 is the only candidacy combining a clear principle, a clean two-author attribution and four decades of independent adoption, and that it is easier to defend in an expert report.
responses.response: I agree with this on attribution and on the defensibility of a single dated paper. I weigh his own reservation about a pure-theory prize with no bridge to life science more heavily than he does. I accept it as a cost, not a disqualification, because the proton-transfer and active-site applications he mentions are where it touches biochemistry. I would also support his proposal to anchor the citation strictly on the 1985 step.

responses.point: Linke asks whether the B012 citation can be defended against the Rothberg, Ju and Mayer routes, and whether B024 can be cited on the 1985 unification alone.
responses.response: On B012 I cannot defend the pair against those routes from the record, and the chair's question has moved me. My round-1 reply on the Solexa chemistry was a judgement about which route was chemically distinct, not a demonstrated priority. On B024 I support fixing the citation to the 1985 unification of electronic structure and ionic motion without adjudicating later work. That answers your concern that the citation honours the concept and not the current tools.

responses.point: Aqvist holds that B024 made bond breaking, proton transfer and liquid water computable without a pre-fitted force field, and that recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I accept the substance. In round 1 I said that clean credit is not higher merit, and I still think so, but he and I now agree the decisive point is whether credit can be assigned defensibly. His own flagged risk of overvaluing theory is fair. I would answer it by noting that quantitative agreement with experiment is what makes B024 a chemistry result and not only a formalism.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first for clinical consequence, with the Cullis, Hope and Madden trio.
responses.response: I still find the pKa-tuned design principle convincing and the clinical validation beyond question. My difficulty remains the cut. The chair's question about priority among Vancouver and MIT work has no documented answer yet, and the 2023 Medicine prize makes the adjacent-field concern real. I would keep B064 off my ballot unless the committee settles whether ionizable-lipid design or rapid-mixing assembly is the decisive step.

uncertainties: Whether B024 will be accepted as chemistry and not as condensed-matter physics, given the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes.
Whether B012 can be defended with a Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair if an expert report resolves the Solexa, 454, Ju and Mayer chronology; I would then reconsider.
Whether B046 (degraders) should be raised to a full candidacy, which depends on resolving credit among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli and Handa and on how much clinical proof is required.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. None of the credited names for B024, B012 or B046 is a collaborator or Umeå colleague. My research is a user of sequencing but this is not a personal tie, and I have no tie to computational chemistry.
